QEVA PRINT CORE 0.5
===================

QEVA is a map and executable instrument for explicit mathematical objects, experiments, evidence, history, and open questions.
The domain and website are replaceable. Preserve exact revisions, provenance, manifests, and the right to fork.

Release: 0.5.0
Current objects: 116
Current experiments: 6
Start with protocol/CORE.txt, archive/current.jsonl, and experiments/current.jsonl.

Five permanent separations:
1. syntax is not semantics
2. derivation is not truth without a model
3. citation is not logical dependence
4. simulation is not proof
5. public access is not redistribution permission

qeva:1:addition@1
Addition
Addition combines counts by repeated successor.

qeva:1:algorithm@1
Algorithm
An algorithm is a finite description of an effective step-by-step procedure for a class of inputs.

qeva:1:attractor@2
Attractor
An attractor is long-run structure toward which many permitted starting states move.

qeva:1:axiom@1
Axiom
An axiom is a declared starting statement or statement scheme of a formal theory.

qeva:1:axiom-choice@1
Axiom of choice
A simultaneous choice can be made from every member of a family of nonempty sets.

qeva:1:axiom-empty-set@1
Axiom of empty set
There exists a set with no members.

qeva:1:axiom-extensionality@1
Axiom of extensionality
Two sets are equal when they have exactly the same members.

qeva:1:axiom-foundation@1
Axiom of foundation
Every nonempty set has a member disjoint from it, blocking ordinary descending membership loops.

qeva:1:axiom-infinity@1
Axiom of infinity
At least one inductive set exists, supplying enough sets to model the natural numbers.

qeva:1:axiom-pairing@1
Axiom of pairing
For any two sets, a set exists whose members are exactly those two sets.

qeva:1:axiom-power-set@1
Axiom of power set
For every set, there is a set containing exactly all of its subsets.

qeva:1:axiom-union@1
Axiom of union
The members of members of a set can be gathered into one set.

qeva:1:bijection@1
Bijection
A bijection pairs two collections without omission or collision.

qeva:1:cardinality@1
Cardinality
Cardinality compares collections by whether their elements can be paired exactly.

qeva:1:category-theoretic-foundations@1
Category-theoretic foundations
Category-theoretic foundations emphasize objects, composable arrows, and invariance under structure-preserving equivalence.

qeva:1:chaos@2
Chaos
“Chaos” has several rigorous definitions. QEVA should name the definition being used instead of treating the word as self-explanatory.

qeva:1:chirality@2
Chirality
A chiral object has a handedness: mirroring changes it in a way that allowed orientation-preserving motions cannot undo.

qeva:1:classical-logic@1
Classical logic
Classical logic is the branch that validates principles such as excluded middle and double-negation elimination.

qeva:1:closed-form@2
Closed form
“Closed form” usually means an explicit formula, but what operations are allowed differs by field and author.

qeva:1:coarse-graining@2
Coarse-graining
Coarse-graining keeps distinctions relevant at one scale or task and merges others.

qeva:1:collatz-conjecture@2
Collatz conjecture
Every tested starting value appears eventually to enter the 1→4→2→1 cycle, but no proof is known for all positive integers.

qeva:1:collatz-map@2
Collatz map
Collatz dynamics repeatedly applies one of two arithmetic rules depending on parity.

qeva:1:completeness@1
Completeness
Completeness can mean that every semantic consequence is provable, or that a space has no missing limits; the meanings must be named.

qeva:1:complex-number@2
Complex number
Represent a complex number by a pair of real coordinates and define arithmetic so that the second coordinate behaves like a square root of minus one.

qeva:1:composition@1
Composition
Composition feeds the output of one map into the input of another.

qeva:1:computability@1
Computability
Computability asks which input-output tasks can be carried out by an idealized finite procedure.

qeva:1:conjunction@1
Conjunction
Conjunction joins requirements that must hold together.

qeva:1:consistency@1
Consistency
A theory is consistent when its rules do not derive an explicit contradiction.

qeva:1:constructive-logic@1
Constructive logic
Constructive logic treats a proof as information and does not accept every classical principle without a construction.

qeva:1:continuity@2
Continuity
A continuous map does not tear apart the chosen topology: inverse images of observable open regions remain open.

qeva:1:decidability@1
Decidability
A decision problem is decidable when one algorithm always halts and returns the correct yes/no answer.

qeva:1:definition@1
Definition
A definition fixes how a new expression is to be used in terms of already available structure.

qeva:1:dependent-type-theory@1
Dependent type theory
Dependent types may vary with terms, letting statements and proofs live in one typed language.

qeva:1:derivability@2
Derivability
Writing Gamma |- P means that P can be reached by a finite sequence of allowed proof steps from the declared axioms and premises.

qeva:1:derivative@1
Derivative
A derivative is the best local linear rate of change when the relevant limit exists.

qeva:1:discreteness@2
Discrete structure
A discrete description treats states as individually separable rather than forcing arbitrarily close intermediate states.

qeva:1:disjunction@1
Disjunction
Disjunction joins alternatives and says that at least one is admitted under the chosen logic.

qeva:1:distinction@1
Distinction
Reasoning begins by allowing one state, mark, or object to be told apart from another.

qeva:1:empty-set@2
Empty set
The empty set has no members. Its existence is theory-relative, and extensionality makes it unique when it exists.

qeva:1:equivalence@2
Equivalence relation
A relation is an equivalence relation when it behaves like equality with respect to reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity.

qeva:1:existential-quantifier@1
Existential quantifier
Existential quantification asserts that at least one permitted witness satisfies a condition.

qeva:1:exploration-exploitation@2
Exploration–exploitation tradeoff
Exploitation uses what currently looks best; exploration spends effort learning whether something else is better.

qeva:1:expression@1
Expression
An expression is a finite arrangement of symbols built by explicit formation rules.

qeva:1:field@1
Field
A field is a commutative arithmetic system where every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.

qeva:1:first-order-logic@1
First-order logic
First-order logic quantifies over objects while keeping predicates and functions in a fixed signature.

qeva:1:fixed-point@2
Fixed point
A fixed point reproduces itself after one application of the update rule.

qeva:1:formal-system@2
Formal system
A formal system fixes the symbols you may write, the starting statements you accept, and the rules by which new statements may be derived.

qeva:1:function@1
Function
A function assigns exactly one output to each permitted input.

qeva:1:graph@1
Graph
A graph records objects and pairwise connections while discarding most other detail.

qeva:1:group@1
Group
A group captures reversible composition with an identity.

qeva:1:group-action@1
Group action
A group action describes how reversible transformations move objects while respecting composition.

qeva:1:grouping@2
Grouping / partition
Grouping makes some distinctions irrelevant by assigning multiple objects to the same class.

qeva:1:halving@2
Halving
“Half of x” is not one universal operation. It depends on what x is and which operations exist in its mathematical structure.

qeva:1:hierarchy@2
Hierarchy and scale
A hierarchical description says what belongs above, below, inside, or at a coarser scale—and how levels connect.

qeva:1:identity@1
Identity
Identity states that two references pick out the same object within a declared framework.

qeva:1:implication@1
Implication
Implication connects a condition to what follows from it.

qeva:1:inference-rule@1
Inference rule
An inference rule licenses a transition from specified premises to a conclusion.

qeva:1:injective-function@1
Injection
An injective function never sends two different inputs to the same output.

qeva:1:integer@1
Integer
Integers extend natural numbers with additive opposites.

qeva:1:invariant@2
Invariant
An invariant deliberately forgets changes that the chosen transformations are allowed to make.

qeva:1:excluded-middle@1
Law of excluded middle
For every statement P, classical logic admits P or not-P.

qeva:1:limit@1
Limit
A limit states that values eventually remain arbitrarily close to a target.

qeva:1:linearity@1
Linearity
A linear map preserves addition and scalar multiplication.

qeva:1:local-global@2
Local versus global optimum
Being unbeatable nearby does not mean being best everywhere.

qeva:1:induction@1
Mathematical induction
Induction proves a property of every natural number from a base case and a successor step.

qeva:1:measure@1
Measure
A measure assigns a nonnegative size to measurable sets while adding the sizes of disjoint pieces.

qeva:1:membership@1
Membership
Membership records that an object is one of the elements of a set.

qeva:1:metric-space@1
Metric space
A metric assigns a distance satisfying nonnegativity, identity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality.

qeva:1:model@1
Model
A model gives symbols a domain and interpretation so statements can be evaluated.

qeva:1:multiplication@1
Multiplication
Multiplication combines equal-sized groups by repeated addition.

qeva:1:natural-number@2
Natural number
First-order Peano arithmetic describes zero, successor, addition, multiplication, and induction through explicit axioms and schemas.

qeva:1:negation@1
Negation
Negation forms a statement that denies another statement under the chosen semantics.

qeva:1:nonlinearity@2
Nonlinearity
In a nonlinear system, combining inputs need not combine outputs by simple superposition.

qeva:1:object@1
Object
An object is whatever a chosen mathematical discourse permits us to refer to as one thing.

qeva:1:one-plus-one@2
One plus one equals two
The kernel expands addition once, then removes addition by zero, leaving exactly the term used to define two.

qeva:1:operation@2
Operation
An operation takes inputs of declared kinds and returns an output of a declared kind; not every useful operation is closed on one set.

qeva:1:optimization@3
Optimization
Optimization first specifies which choices are allowed and how they are scored; the best lower score may or may not be achieved by a choice.

qeva:1:order@1
Order
An order records a consistent notion of before, below, or no greater than.

qeva:1:ordered-pair@1
Ordered pair
An ordered pair stores two objects while preserving which is first and which is second.

qeva:1:parity@3
Parity
An integer is even when it is twice an integer and odd when it is one more than twice an integer.

qeva:1:periodicity@2
Periodicity of a sequence
A periodic sequence repeats exactly after some fixed positive number of steps.

qeva:1:prime@3
Prime number
A prime is greater than one and cannot be written as a product except using one or itself.

qeva:1:probability-space@1
Probability space
A probability space assigns normalized weight to measurable events.

qeva:1:proof@1
Proof
A proof is a finite, checkable chain from admitted premises to a conclusion under declared rules.

qeva:1:quasiperiodicity@2
Quasiperiodicity
A common quasiperiodic model combines several angular motions whose basic frequencies are rationally independent. The representation itself must be distinguished from the extra conditions needed to guarantee that the resulting function is nonperiodic.

qeva:1:random-variable@1
Random variable
A random variable converts outcomes into measurable values.

qeva:1:rational@1
Rational number
Rational numbers represent ratios of integers with nonzero denominator.

qeva:1:real-number@1
Real number
Real numbers complete the rationals so convergent measurement processes need not leave gaps.

qeva:1:recurrence@2
Recurrence relation
A recurrence describes how values are linked across index steps. It need not always determine a unique sequence unless enough initial data and uniqueness conditions are supplied.

qeva:1:relation@1
Relation
A relation records which tuples of objects stand in a chosen connection.

qeva:1:integral@2
Riemann integral
Cut an interval into sufficiently short pieces, sample the function in each piece, and add height times width; one stable limiting value is the Riemann integral.

qeva:1:ring@1
Ring
A ring supports addition, multiplication, and additive inverses under compatible laws.

qeva:1:satisfaction@2
Satisfaction
A formula can be true in one mathematical structure and false in another. QEVA must name the semantics or model when it uses semantic truth.

qeva:1:schema-replacement@1
Schema of replacement
The image of a set under a definable single-valued correspondence is a set.

qeva:1:schema-separation@1
Schema of separation
A definable condition can select a subset of an already existing set.

qeva:1:information@2
Self-information
Within a probability model, a less probable event carries more self-information when surprise is measured logarithmically.

qeva:1:sensitivity@2
Sensitive dependence on initial conditions
Sensitivity formalizes one kind of error amplification: no matter how closely two starting states are chosen, some nearby state can eventually move a definite distance away.

qeva:1:sequence@2
Sequence
A sequence is not merely a written list; mathematically it is a function whose input is an index.

qeva:1:set@1
Set
A set is a collection treated extensionally: its members determine it.

qeva:1:entropy@1
Shannon entropy
Entropy is the expected self-information of a random variable's distribution.

qeva:1:sigma-algebra@1
Sigma-algebra
A sigma-algebra is a collection of events stable under complementation and countable combination.

qeva:1:signal-noise@2
Signal and noise
Signal is the part treated as informative for a task; noise is the part treated as nuisance, uncertainty, or unresolved variation.

qeva:1:stability@3
Stability
A fixed point is Lyapunov-stable when starting close enough guarantees staying as close as requested forever.

qeva:1:statement@1
Statement
A statement is an expression eligible to be asserted, denied, proved, or evaluated in a model.

qeva:1:subset@1
Subset
A is a subset of B when every member of A is also a member of B.

qeva:1:successor@1
Successor
Successor moves from one natural number to the next.

qeva:1:surjective-function@1
Surjection
A surjective function reaches every element of its declared codomain.

qeva:1:symbol@1
Symbol
A symbol is an atomic mark or token admitted by a formal language.

qeva:1:symmetry@2
Symmetry
Symmetry is never just “looks the same”: one must specify which transformations are allowed and what counts as unchanged.

qeva:1:theorem@1
Theorem
A theorem is a statement accompanied by a valid derivation from declared assumptions in a declared system.

qeva:1:topological-space@1
Topological space
A topology declares which regions count as open, encoding nearness without requiring numerical distance.

qeva:1:type@1
Type
A type classifies expressions and states which constructions may be formed with them.

qeva:1:universal-quantifier@1
Universal quantifier
Universal quantification requires a statement to hold for every permitted value in a domain.

qeva:1:vector-space@1
Vector space
A vector space supports vector addition and scalar multiplication under compatibility laws.

qeva:1:zero@1
Zero
Zero is the distinguished starting value for one common construction of the natural numbers.

qeva:1:zfc-set-theory@1
ZFC set theory
ZFC is a major foundational theory whose objects are sets governed by explicit axiom schemes and axioms.
